pr.title: Add requests to the inbox for work only the person can do
pr.head: 77b84ddba4b67145437740f5184c13cca9f33c11

summary: Projector's inbox is where an agent puts things in front of you while it keeps working. Until now it held two kinds of item: a question, which you answer and whose answer goes back to the agent, and a notice, which you read and dismiss. Each session keeps its items as JSON files under Projector's state directory, and Projector's panel, above the Claude Code prompt, lists them.

Some work only you can do: running a command the agent may not run, signing in to a service, or checking a build on your phone. Agents stitched that hand-off together from a question, a notice, and typed messages. This pull request adds a third kind of item, a request, that carries the work and its outcome as one item.

1. An agent posts a request with project inbox request or the request tool. Its one-line subject says what to do, and its detail holds the steps.
  2. You open its drawer in the panel. It shows the steps, then Done on 1 and Declined on 2 where a question shows its options.
  3. Done or Declined fills your prompt with the quoted request and the word, so you can type notes under it. Sending the prompt records the outcome and carries your notes to the agent.
  4. From a terminal, project inbox done and decline record the outcome, and the panel's deliverer sends the agent DONE or DECLINED.

This is layer 1 of the inbox/requests plan. Layer 2, a later pull request, adds a start action: something the agent must prepare before you can begin, such as installing a build, which waits for you to press start. So the plan moves from ready to in-progress here.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Outcome: how you resolved a request, done or declined, with an optional line of text.
  • Deliverer: the panel's loop, or project inbox watch, that sends an agent the line its item owes, such as DONE 5 Test the gutters → All good.
  • Claim: a short-lived lock a deliverer takes on an item before sending its line, so two deliverers never send it twice.
  • Ask rule: a Claude Code permission rule that makes an agent ask you before running a command, even one an allow rule such as Bash(project *) covers.
  • Agents block: the section project init writes into each repository's AGENTS.md, versioned so init can tell when to rewrite it.

cards.title: Where review stands
cards.html:
• The full gate passed at this head: 1111 unit tests, project check, both plugin validations, 164 hooks tests, the type check, and git diff --check.
  • One finding is open: the agents block's edit leaves unwrapped lines, which every adopting repository's AGENTS.md copies.
  • Until you run project init again, Bash(project *) still lets an agent run done and decline without asking, as the plan's rollout says.

groups.title: A request in the inbox store and the CLI
groups.kicker: The new kind, its outcomes, and the commands that record them
intro: The inbox store keeps one JSON file per item, and every command changes an item under the session's lock. A request is a third kind in that store, so it shares the session's numbering, snoozing, withdrawing, restoring, and delivery with questions and notices.

A request's outcome lives in the same answer field a question's answer does. done records {done: true}. decline records a dismissal with declined: true, so restore and the code that reads a dismissed item work unchanged. Both take an optional one-line --text, which the deliverer appends after an arrow.

groups.title: Only you record a request's outcome
groups.kicker: Ask rules for done and decline, and an allowance for request
intro: Projector's permission rules let an agent run any project command freely, except a few that record the person's own choice. Those are ask rules, which Claude Code checks before allow rules. done and decline join answer, dismiss, and snooze there, so an agent can't mark its own request done. The panel runs these commands itself, outside any agent's shell, so you are never asked when you use it.

The rules reach your settings only when project init runs again. Until then, Bash(project *) allows both commands, as the plan's rollout and the pull request body say. Codex's rules allow request and leave done and decline to its usual approval.

groups.title: The panel's drawer, prompt reading, and tools
groups.kicker: How Claude Code shows a request and reads your Done or Declined
intro: The hooks module is Projector's Claude Code plugin code: it draws the panel, registers the inbox tools agents call, and reads each prompt you send. A request's drawer draws Done and Declined where a question draws its options. Pressing one fills the prompt with the quoted request, a blank line, and the word, and records nothing yet.

When you send the prompt, readPrompt decides what it says to each open item. A quoted request takes an outcome only when the first non-blank line under the quote is exactly Done or Declined; the rest is your notes. Anything else, such as done?, is a reply that leaves the request open. The prompt hook then runs done or decline, followed by claim and delivered, because the prompt itself carried the outcome and notes to the agent.

groups.title: What every agent reads
groups.kicker: The agents block names request beside ask and tell
intro: project init writes a versioned block into each repository's AGENTS.md, which Claude Code and Codex agents both read. The block moves to version 19 so agents learn to post work only you can do with request, and to expect DONE or DECLINED back. A test pins each version's hash, so a later edit can't change a released block silently.

checks.text: Compared this repository's AGENTS.md block with the template, with {projects_dir} as docs/projects: byte-identical. The pinned hash for version 19 matches the template's SHA-256.

Open finding: this line runs to 122 characters, line 78 breaks after five words, and line 87 runs to 89, where the rest of the block wraps at about 76. Rewrap before version 19 ships, run project init, and re-pin the hash; afterwards a fix needs version 20.
